# PythonExport

Source: [`Kernel/PythonExport.wl`](../../Kernel/PythonExport.wl) · Design notes: [MODULES.md](../MODULES.md#pythonexport-kernelpythonexportwl--exportpython)

ExportPython: write an LO Adimensional stage as a Python module for BMWflow's generic adapter (contract: docs/handoff/BMWflow\_LO.md = design/LOPIPELINE.md section 6). Pure numpy + math, elementwise, no state, no value-dependent branching. The loop measure is not in the module: the adapter applies it. Objective, assumptions and checks: docs/MODULES.md section "PythonExport".

## Symbols

### `ExportPython`

`ExportPython[adim, "G" -> alamk^2, "Model" -> "KPZ", "File" -> ".../eqs/KPZ_LO.py"]` writes the LO (or NLO: APPROXIMATION "NLO", loop and linear with the external frequency w, contract v4) Adimensional stage as a Python module (constants CONTRACT\_VERSION, FUNCTIONS, ETAS, COUPLINGS, SHAPES, P2\_DIVIDED, FIXED\_DIMENSION, APPROXIMATION, MODEL; functions linear, loop, eta\_matrix, eta\_vector, beta; docs/handoff/BMWflow\_LO.md) and returns its path. "G" is BMWflow's scalar coupling g in terms of the single exported coupling: every kernel is written in g (COUPLINGS = ("g",)) and beta is d\_s g. "Model" is a label (MODEL).

### `PythonParts`

`PythonParts[adim]` gives the exported expressions with the Python argument names as placeholders `PythonVariable["fq", i]` etc. (Mathematica expressions, as ExportPython prints them): &lt;\|"linear" -> ..., "loop" -> ..., ...\|>. `PythonParts[adim, G]` writes them in g = G: `PythonVariable["couplings", 0]` is then g and "beta" is {d\_s g}.

### `PythonAtom`

`PythonAtom["fQ", i, "rQ", j]` in PythonParts is the propagator atom `fQ[i]` + `rQ[j]` (printed as that sum): function i and the regulator shape j of its Gamma2 entry. The loop is written in atoms so that large r(q), r(Q) do not cancel numerically.

### `PythonVariable`

`PythonVariable[name]` or `PythonVariable[name, i]` is the Python argument name (`name[i]`, 0-based) in PythonParts.
